title: Negotiating Terms Over Price (The Contrarian Playbook)
rules: Golden Rule: 'You name the price; I name the terms.' If the seller insists on an inflated price ($1.2M on an $800k business), agree to the price ONLY if structured with a 10-year low-interest seller note or earnout.
Solve the Seller's Real Pain: Retiring owners often care more about employee legacy, avoiding a lump-sum IRS tax hit, and guaranteed monthly retirement checks than raw enterprise valuation.
Silence as Power: When an unrealistic counter-offer is made, remain quiet. The first person to speak after a pause concedes leverage.
Earn-Out Safety Net: Tie 20-30% of the purchase price to customer retention and revenue stability over months 12-24.
